Hi Klemens,

We also found the annotation in the TKO paper is inconsistent with the raw data. So we updated the annotation: ftp://massive.ucsd.edu/RMSV000000267/2020-06-06_mnchoi_42177bd3/metadata/. 

The FTP for TKO-1mix data is publicly accessible on our side. Did you try this link: https://massive.ucsd.edu/ProteoSAFe/reanalysis.jsp?task=42177bd31a4d45f98790019f7fe1fcf9?

Best,
Ting

On Monday, January 11, 2021 at 2:43:12 PM UTC-5 froehlic...@gmail.com wrote:
Dear MSstats Developer

I am currently trying to reanalyze some data in preparation for a tutorial on msstatsTMT (Galaxy Tutorial with Melanie Föll).
I chose the small triple KO yeast experiment reanalyzed here:
" MSstatsTMT: Statistical detection of differentially abundant proteins in experiments with isobaric labeling and multiple mixtures "

I ran into 2 problems:
I think the Gigi lab annotation is incorrect, or my MaxQuant is counting the channels in a different way since the knockouts are clearly visible in different channels. To confirm this I wanted to have a look at your R scripts which should be available here:
  TKO-1mix data (MassIVE.quant reanalyses container identifier: RMSV000000267) 
But the FTP does not seem to be public/available at least I cannot access it, although I can access other massive directories. Am I doing something wrong and other people can access it?

Could you please provide me with the complete data analysis of this part? The data is really nice and it would be awesome to have consistent data in these tutorials. 

Best Klemens
